answers.core:
This should be core because of the large number of possible use cases, including :
- Using it as a true 3D perspective background in a 2D game
- Using it as a skybox with animation and dynamic properties
- Using it as a 3D background with 3D games
- Dynamic muiti-layered background effects using more than one background scene

Additionally this is a very common feature in commercial game engines (camera layers)
answers.workaround:
As far as I know it's impossible because there is no simple way to render "panoramic backgrounds" and use them as background of camera.
The simplest workaround I can imagine would be to render the 6 faces of a cubemap, build a cubemap texture, convert it to an equirectangular projection (via a shader ?) and then use it as a background sky.
This is not doable in a few lines of script, and the performance would probably be really poor ...
